CircularEconomy.audienceTitle: Which problem do you need to solve?

audiences.question: What is stopping us from preparing this pickup?
audiences.answer: Battery record, packaging, selected packages, collector and delivery site: the information is brought together before creating the packing list.

audiences.question: How can owners and service providers work on the same records?
audiences.answer: A declaration workflow for the network, management interfaces for internal teams and exchanges with treatment centers. Access rules follow each party’s responsibilities.

audiences.question: Which processing price and logistics cost were accepted?
audiences.answer: Proposals retain their price components, author, date and status. Their history shows the terms discussed and those agreed.

audiences.question: Does the record contain the right code, documents and required signatures?
audiences.answer: EWC codes, battery diagnostics, documents and waste tracking statuses are handled within the workflow. Application controls make required items and incomplete steps visible.

audiences.question: Which information should be exchanged with existing systems?
audiences.answer: Battery data, status changes and accepted offers can flow to partner systems through APIs and notifications. Integration is defined for each business object and its access rights.

CircularEconomy.scopeTitle: A focused module or a complete application.

scopeItems.title: Extend an existing tool
scopeItems.text: Your logistics software works, but declarations arrive by email? The project can focus on collecting the information and passing it to that system.

scopeItems.title: Rework a limiting workflow
scopeItems.text: Your network already uses an application? We examine the data, rules and exchanges to preserve before extending or replacing the relevant part.

scopeItems.title: Build an end-to-end service
scopeItems.text: You are setting up a new take-back activity? We can develop the network portal, administration tools and exchanges needed with partners.

faqs.question: Is this an off-the-shelf software product?
faqs.answer: We design and develop custom applications. The examples show features we have already built; together we define which ones meet your needs, which rules to adapt and which systems to connect.

faqs.question: Do we have to replace our existing tools (ERP, transport, MES, billing, etc.)?
faqs.answer: The first step is to establish what is already covered. An integration or complementary module may be enough. We check exchange capabilities with your IT teams before agreeing on scope.

faqs.question: Does the application guarantee regulatory compliance?
faqs.answer: It implements the controls and document exchanges defined for the project. Waste classification, transport rules and applicable obligations must be validated by the responsible specialists. An EWC code or a Trackdechets connection alone does not guarantee compliance.

faqs.question: Do you only work with vehicles and batteries?
faqs.answer: These are the industries illustrated here by our projects. For another activity, we examine similarities and differences: products or materials, stakeholders, documents, transactions and existing tools. Relevance depends on the operations to support.

faqs.question: Where does AI fit?
faqs.answer: When a need involves reading documents, extracting information or supporting assessment, we can explore an AI component. Not all the features in these guides depend on AI: API-based identification, input rules and status exchanges already address concrete needs.

CircularEconomy.ctaText: Show us a real flow, its participants and the tools already in place.

dossiers.label: End-of-life vehicles
dossiers.title: Identify the vehicle. Complete the record. Organize take-back.
dossiers.summary: License plate or VIN, retrieved specifications, administrative documents and interfaces for the take-back network.
dossiers.description: An individual or a garage starts by declaring a vehicle. Behind that form, teams need reliable information, prepared documents and a request they can pass to the parties handling collection. Here are the functions we have developed to connect these steps.
dossiers.context: Project example: a vehicle take-back platform with individual and professional workflows connected to an existing management system.

sections.title: Start with a plate or VIN, not an empty record.
sections.situation: Asking users to reenter a vehicle’s make, model and specifications adds fields to complete and corrections to handle later.
actions: The declarant provides the country and available identifier: a license plate or VIN, the vehicle identification number.
The application queries an identification service and populates the record with the returned specifications.
The user is asked to complete required fields that remain empty. Manual entry is available when data cannot be retrieved.
sections.rule: The identification method and required fields vary by country. The integration does not assume that every lookup returns a complete record.
sections.result: A structured vehicle record with available specifications retrieved and missing information completed.

sections.title: Move the administrative record forward with the request.
sections.situation: A take-back request is not ready to process simply because the vehicle has been identified. It also includes declarative information and documents.
actions: The workflow brings together the information and documents needed to handle the request.
The team finds these items in the vehicle record rather than in separate exchanges.
Generation and electronic signing of transfer and destruction documents are integrated into the process for the relevant French operations.
sections.rule: Document content and signature steps depend on the country and procedure. The project uses the applicable documents and defines the expected signatories.
sections.result: The request, supporting documents and signature tracking are linked to the relevant vehicle.

sections.title: Give the network a shared operational tool.
sections.situation: Owners, garages, end-of-life vehicle treatment centers and program teams act at different times with different responsibilities.
actions: Separate workflows support individual and professional requests.
Management interfaces let teams and partners follow vehicles and handling steps.
Connections to the existing system exchange the information needed between declaration, collection and tracking through dismantling.
sections.rule: The public portal and professional tool serve different uses. Screens and access rights need to reflect that separation.
sections.result: Vehicle-level tracking and interfaces suited to the people declaring, handling and managing operations.

dossiers.label: Batteries, collection & recovery
dossiers.title: A battery to handle, with its specifications, constraints and take-back terms.
dossiers.summary: EWC code, condition and diagnostics, packing lists, processing and transport prices, receiving and treatment tracking.
dossiers.description: A battery is more than a reference and a pickup address. Its type, condition, documents and agreed terms affect handling. We have developed the modules below across recycling and second-life projects.
dossiers.context: Examples from several applications developed for an automotive manufacturer and a battery recycler. The modules are presented together to explain the operations they support.

sections.title: Identify the battery and record its waste code.
sections.situation: The reference data combines model, VIN or BIN, condition, charge, health, dimensions and weight. The declaration completes these characteristics with EWC and UN codes, evidence and photos.
actions: The declaration links the battery to its type and owner information.
The workflow suggests an EWC code — from the European waste classification — using the existing declaration or reference battery type.
The declarant can select or correct the code. It is saved in the record and changes are available in the history.
sections.rule: Prefilled information comes from reference data. It does not replace validation of the waste classification by the responsible stakeholders.
sections.result: A battery characterized in a record ready for collection, transport and traceability.

sections.title: Capture battery condition before collection.
sections.situation: A damaged battery requires different preparation from a battery in another condition. Stakeholders need diagnostics and relevant documents before organizing the next steps.
actions: The declarant records battery condition and attaches the diagnostic and checklist documents required by the workflow.
ADR transport information associated with the selected condition is shown in the interface.
General photos and, depending on the declaring party and identifier readability, a serial-number photo are requested.
sections.rule: Required documents depend on context. Transport and packaging rules are defined with the responsible specialists; the portal does not infer them from a photograph.
sections.result: A record bringing together declared condition, photos and documents needed to assess handling.

sections.title: Build a consistent packing list.
sections.situation: Several declarations and packages may be ready to leave. Selecting them without considering the collector or delivery site can produce a list that does not fit the intended operation.
actions: Users review declarations with their owner, collector, delivery site, chemistry, packaging and status.
They select the packages to include in the packing list.
In the developed workflow, selection prevents mixing delivery sites or collectors incompatible with the current grouping.
sections.rule: This grouping check is an explicit business rule. For your organization, we define the criteria that permit or prevent a shared departure.
sections.result: A packing list linked to declarations, packaging, palletization and the planned transport.

sections.title: Separate processing price from logistics cost.
sections.situation: Negotiation with a provider may cover both battery processing and transport. A single amount does not capture the terms of the agreement.
actions: A proposal includes processing price, logistics price, currency and an optional comment.
Successive proposals are kept with their author, date and acceptance or refusal status.
Offer operations are also available to providers through an API. Notifications can inform their system when an offer is created or accepted.
sections.rule: This example covers price negotiation for batteries and pickup groups. A trading arrangement involving multiple purchase and resale contracts would require specific scoping.
sections.result: Proposed and agreed terms remain available with the record, without searching an email chain for the latest agreement.

sections.title: Connect collection, receiving and treatment.
sections.situation: A battery reported as collected must then be received and tracked through treatment. Document status may also condition which actions are available in the tool.
actions: Statuses distinguish batteries ready for pickup, collected, received and processed.
In a workflow connected to Trackdechets, receiving records a date and receiver’s name, then updates the linked waste tracking form and declaration.
Partners can be notified of status changes to update their own tracking.
sections.rule: Physical and document tracking are linked but remain distinct. The workflow shows the stage reached and the actions still required.
sections.result: A declaration tracked after departure from the owner’s site, with associated steps and documents.
data: Linked waste tracking form, where applicable

dossiers.label: Documents & integrations
dossiers.title: Keep information and documents connected to operations.
dossiers.summary: EWC, ADR, Trackdechets waste tracking, signatures and API exchanges: what the applications handle and where your systems fit.
dossiers.description: Operations often involve several applications. The business record needs to retain useful references, track document stages and send events to partners. Here are integrations and controls we have developed.
dossiers.context: Examples from vehicle and battery projects. Document obligations and integration capabilities must be checked for each country, activity and system involved.

sections.title: EWC and ADR: separate information, separate purposes.
sections.situation: Waste classification codes and transport information need to be recorded in the right place. Grouping them under a compliance label does not explain what the tool actually does.
actions: The EWC code is linked to the declaration and can be suggested from the reference battery type.
Battery condition is recorded separately with the required diagnostic documents.
The interface displays the ADR information defined for that condition. Teams define input rules, supporting documents and required approvals.
sections.rule: The application organizes data and applies defined rules. It does not automatically turn an EWC code into authorization for transport or treatment.
sections.result: Distinct, accessible information that helps qualified stakeholders review the record.

sections.title: Include the waste tracking form in declaration tracking.
sections.situation: For relevant French operations, the waste tracking form (BSD) has its own statuses. Teams need to know whether it is created, signed and ready for the next step.
actions: The application creates or updates a form through Trackdechets and stores its identifier with the declaration.
It checks status and distinguishes a missing producer signature from a missing collector signature.
The workflow can condition receiving on these signatures, then transmit receiving and treatment information.
sections.rule: A blocked step should explain why and who needs to resolve it. This describes a control in the developed workflow, not a universal legal rule.
sections.result: The form and declaration remain linked; the user sees document status and required actions.

sections.title: Link signatures to the right record.
sections.situation: A document sent for signature should remain connected to the vehicle or operation that generated it.
actions: In the relevant vehicle workflows, transfer and destruction documents are generated within the process.
The DocuSign electronic signature service is integrated into the workflow.
The business record provides access to the documents and signature progress.
sections.rule: Signatories, documents and signature timing are defined by the procedure. The project also accounts for incomplete steps.
sections.result: Continuity between the request, prepared documents and signature tracking.

sections.title: Exchange business objects, not just files.
sections.situation: A provider may already manage operations in its own system. Requiring every change to be entered again in a portal adds work instead of removing it.
actions: A provider API supports operations including battery data exports and imports and price proposals.
Outgoing notifications report specific events: a battery assigned, ready for pickup, received or processed; an offer created or accepted.
Access is authenticated and limited to the partner’s scope. Interfaces and exchange formats are defined for the relevant operations.
sections.rule: A connection to your ERP or logistics software needs assessment: available data, exchange direction, access rights and error handling. We do not assume a universal connector exists.
sections.result: A partner can update tracking from its system and receive events relevant to its operations.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.content:
Legal framework – compliance with GDPR and French law

FDTI Consulting declares that the company processes personal data in accordance with Regulation (EU) 2016/679 of the European Parliament and of the Council of April 27, 2016, relating to the protection of natural persons with regard to the processing of personal data and the free movement of such data (hereinafter referred to as the GDPR) and French law n° 78-17 of January 6, 1978 relating to data processing, files and freedoms.


On May 25, 2018, the General Data Protection Regulations entered into force. Companies dealing with data must now ensure optimal data protection at all times and be able to demonstrate it by documenting their compliance.


In view of its activity, FDTI Consulting may need to process personal data collected and processed by its customers. The following elements are intended to define internal processing rules at FDTI Consulting and guarantee compliance with personal data in accordance with the GDPR.


In all of its activities, FDTI Consulting considers the protection of personal data to be fundamental and strives as soon as possible to anonymize all the data it processes and to ensure the non-disclosure of data outside the reference legal frameworks.

Governance

The data processed by FDTI never leaves the European Union and is not subject to any jurisdiction outside the European Union.


Our host OVH France is located in France and hosts our services in France. Therefore they are not subject to the Cloud Act

Personal data processing process

Except in special cases, FDTI Consulting does not need personal data to carry out its missions. FDTI Consulting therefore asks its clients not to send it any personal data. In the event of unexpected receipt of personal data, FDTI Consulting will directly destroy this data and notify the sender.


Some personal data may be useful for identification purposes. In this case, FDTI Consulting will ask the data provider to pseudonymize this data. FDTI Consulting will support this pseudonymization.

In the event that the sender hasn't the technical capacities or the human capacities to carry out this pseudonymization in his environment, FDTI Consulting will take care of it. Only one person within FDTI Consulting will therefore have access to this personal data, in order to pseudonymize it and distribute this pseudonymized data within FDTI Consulting.


All personal data used in the context of our work is thus stored in a secure space and respects the consent given by the persons concerned. All this data is then permanently deleted, following the studies and processing necessary for the conduct of our various projects.

page_tags.title: Work | Data, AI & Application Projects - FDTI
page_tags.description: Real-world implementations: court automation with AI, circular economy platforms, battery marketplaces, smart city lighting, social media analytics with LLMs, data warehouses for retail and justice sectors.

use_case_list.title: AI platform for commercial courts
use_case_list.challenge: A software vendor for court clerks wanted to embed AI directly into its platform to optimize processing time and accuracy for specific time-consuming clerk tasks.
use_case_list.approach: Modular architecture structured by AI use cases (tailored LLMs). On-prem FastAPI AI stack, fully integrated into the existing tool via API, but also accessible to other users via secure API. TypeScript/SvelteKit portal.
use_case_list.impact: AI pre-analysis runs in parallel with business workflows: around 40 billion tokens processed per year on a first use case, with a significant time-saving equivalent while meeting judicial confidentiality requirements.
details: Critical use cases covered: case summaries, dossier validation, automated extraction of sensitive documents.
Deployment inside the client's VPN with fine-grained monitoring and contractual SLAs.
Self-service portal to generate API keys, track usage and troubleshoot calls.
Re-annotation loops to improve models plus full audit tooling.
Enablement plan with trainings, playbooks and dedicated support.
TypeScript/SvelteKit front-end delivering a frictionless experience alongside legacy tools.

use_case_list.title: End-of-life vehicle management platform
use_case_list.challenge: Following the creation of Valorauto, a joint venture between Stellantis and Galloo, the circular-economy platform needed to modernize its existing tool to manage end-of-life vehicle take-back processes (B2B and B2C) and track each vehicle journey from owner collection to vehicle dismantling.
use_case_list.approach: Development of the Valorauto portal with declaration, administration and vehicle-tracking interfaces across the different stakeholders, business workflows and Azure Functions APIs deployed on the client Azure infrastructure (MSSQL databases, Azure Service Bus) to orchestrate an existing .NET stack connecting owners and ELV centers.
use_case_list.impact: End-to-end traceability supporting the group circular-economy branch, with a network of more than 5,000 partner companies and a response to the manufacturer obligations related to Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR).
details: End-to-end development of the platform, databases and APIs.
Complete declaration workflow design for dealers, repair centers and private owners.
Azure Functions APIs connecting the group logistics, CRM and finance systems.
API interconnection with the wider circular-economy ecosystem (recyclers, owners, buyers, eco-organizations).
Real-time mapping of material flows and automatic generation of regulatory documents.
Multi-brand management: local rules, catalogs and pricing by country.
Azure infrastructure sized for regulatory peaks and audits.
Operational and regulatory dashboards consolidating B2B and B2C flows.
Personalized email notifications for every user (garages, dealers, private owners) at each workflow step.

use_case_list.title: Battery reuse marketplace
use_case_list.challenge: An automotive manufacturer needed a central tool to manage the collection, recycling and resale of its batteries, in collaboration with its partners and buyers. The tool had to manage complete process traceability to meet regulatory requirements related to the structuring of EPR (Extended Producer Responsibility) systems.
use_case_list.approach: Web marketplace connected to partner ERPs, acting as a logistics and matchmaking platform. End-to-end traceability and automated flows to buyers or recyclers, price and terms negotiation with partners integrated in the app. The entire process can be managed from the portal or via the API.
use_case_list.impact: Several thousand batteries redirected each month by hundreds of owners and service providers, with centralized reporting for authorities and administration interface for client employees. Seamless integration of the solution into the ecosystem.
details: End-to-end platform development, databases and APIs.
Full declaration process for end-of-life batteries plus automatic logistics documents.
API integrations with recyclers and eco-organizations to track pickups, tests and certificates, price offers.
Buyer workspace to source reusable batteries and manage the transaction.
Quality/compliance scoring with shared SLAs.
Regulatory reporting exportable in one click.
Automated email notifications for partners and buyers across pickup, testing and resale steps.
Identity federation through Keycloak for group entities and external partners.

use_case_list.title: Operations platform for a battery recycler
use_case_list.challenge: A recycler needed one tool for battery declarations, preliminary review, collection preparation, tracking records, reception and treatment steps.
use_case_list.approach: Development of a business application connecting declarations, battery reference data, packing lists, grouping controls, Trackdechets records and reception actions.
use_case_list.impact: Teams follow each file from declaration to treatment, with explicit controls over collectors, destination sites, signatures and document statuses.
details: Declaration qualification based on battery chemistry, sub-chemistry and typology.
Packing lists that prevent incompatible collectors or destination sites from being grouped together.
Trackdechets record creation and updates, with visibility into expected signatures.
Declaration reception and treatment stages followed in the same business record.
Interfaces suited to internal teams and collection partners.

use_case_list.title: Public lighting supervision
use_case_list.challenge: A client specialized in public lighting management for municipalities and their service providers needed a single platform to manage public lighting, adjust schedules, detect anomalies and plan maintenance.
use_case_list.approach: Development of a web application serving as a management portal and analysis dashboards. AWS S3 + DuckDB/Parquet real-time stack, Shell/Cron pipelines, FastAPI backend and TypeScript/SvelteKit UI.
use_case_list.impact: The application is consulted every morning by network managers. Consumption and incident measurements are dynamically adjusted, with predictive maintenance and alerting deployed across more than 40 territories.
details: Continuous collection of lighting meters with optimized S3 + Parquet storage.
Shell/Cron pipelines to refresh the cache.
DuckDB analytics delivering KPIs instantly over multi-year history, with dynamic visualizations to display results.
Mandate management system for data owners and users.
Alert dashboards for operators (failures, consumption, schedule anomalies).
Open REST API to plug operator and city systems.
Multi-tenant management with granular permissions and per-city segmentation.

use_case_list.title: AI analysis of social media campaigns
use_case_list.challenge: The NGO needed to compare environmental narratives on Facebook and Instagram to guide communications investments.
use_case_list.approach: LLM methodology (ChatGPT + tailored prompts) scoring tone/topics/perspectives, correlated with Facebook/Instagram KPIs by audience type (age, country, interests) and yielding comparative visuals.
use_case_list.impact: Budget reallocation per country/platform and an internalized analysis framework.
details: Prompts capturing tone, actors, topics and emotions on Facebook/Instagram.
Automated pipeline: social data → LLM → scoring of topics/tones/perspectives per audience type.
Cross-analysis with post performance to recommend priority themes.
Documented methodology replicable by local teams.
Enablement sessions to interpret recommendations and adjust budgets.

use_case_list.title: Data hub & NLP
use_case_list.challenge: Centralize customer review flows from an electronics leader in France and industrialize their analysis with AI and dashboards.
use_case_list.approach: Pipelines to collect data from various providers and collection managers via API Airflow→BigQuery, GCP governance, NLP (HuggingFace, BERTopic, QA, LLM), delivery in Tableau dashboards and internal data distribution to other concerned teams.
use_case_list.impact: Customer service instantly retrieves classified topics, escalated alerts and tracks requests more precisely. The product team identifies and anticipates defects and logistics issues. The legal team anticipates litigation.
details: Multi-API collection (mystery shopping, CRM, social, reviews) orchestrated by Airflow.
Cloud policies: team segmentation, data localization, security and best practices.
Analysis and classification pipeline with LLMs.
NLP pipelines for similarity, sentiment and topics across multiple languages.
Design and implementation of dashboards used daily by the Customer & Market insights team.
Documentation and training for data/business teams.
Automated insight exports to marketing BUs and agencies.

use_case_list.title: Near real-time data warehouse
use_case_list.challenge: As part of an ERP migration, migrate 98 high-volume JSON business objects with complex structures (shops, warehouses, users, receipts, stocks...) from Azure to Snowflake to feed Qlik in near real-time.
use_case_list.approach: Automatic generation of hundreds of SQL and Scala queries from specifications to denest complex objects. The system produced and feeds 150+ tables and views updated in real-time. ADLS→Snowflake ingestion via Kafka/ADF and orchestration via streams and tasks.
use_case_list.impact: Minute-level feeds for BI teams processing millions of files per day. Transition to the new analysis system followed by deprecation of the legacy one.
details: Automatic SQL generation from XML metadata to speed up deployments.
Delta updates orchestrated by Snowflake Tasks with dedicated monitoring.
